root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `reset_frame_buffers()` calls `set_planes_to_neutral_grey()` on a slot, that slot must still own a live raw frame buffer (`frame_bufs[i].raw_frame_buffer.priv != NULL`). Released slots whose ownership callback cleared `priv` must not be repainted.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the crashing path, `reset_frame_buffers()` releases non-current slots through `release_fb_cb` and then immediately repaints one of those released wrappers anyway. The stale slot reaches the neutral-grey call with `frame_bufs[i].raw_frame_buffer.priv == NULL`, proving the repaint runs on a slot whose backing frame buffer is no longer owned. The fixed program only repaints the live current slot, so the same call executes with a live owner.

nodes.state: When the reusable internal frame buffer is too small, `av1_get_frame_buffer()` frees `int_fb_list->int_fb[i].data`; any stale `RefCntBuffer` wrapper still caching that raw pointer now names freed storage.
`set_planes_to_neutral_grey()` converts `buf->buffers[plane]` into `base` and performs the AddressSanitizer-reported high-bitdepth write through the stale buffer wrapper.

edges.relation: The raw pointer freed in `av1_get_frame_buffer()` remains cached in the later repainted slot as `frame_bufs[i].raw_frame_buffer.data`, so the repaint runs after the free on the same underlying storage.
The same stale YV12 buffer backing selected at `reset_frame_buffers()` reaches `set_planes_to_neutral_grey()` unchanged, carrying the stale allocation into the crashing neutral-grey write.
